sentences.text: This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.
2. Brief case of the petitioner in the nutshell:
It is the case of the petitioners that, on 01.11.2023 at about 2.15 p.m., when the deceased Rathnamma H.A. was proceeding on the motor cycle bearing Reg.

No.KA-52-V- 7991 as pillion rider near Kuluvanahalli village, Bengaluru- Tumkuru NH-48 Road, Nelamangala, at that time, the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-34-F-1445 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased motor cycle from behind.
As a result of impact the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over her body and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
Immediately after the accident she was shifted to Government Hospital at Nelamangala, wherein Post mortem was conducted and the corpse was handed over to the family members.
The petitioners have spent huge amount towards Conveyance, Death Ceremony, Obsequies and etc.

It is further urged that prior to the accident, deceased Rathnamma H.A. was hale and healthy and working doing vegetable business and agriculture and earning Rs.30,000/- per month and because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.
It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus and respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

2
Hence prayed to allow the petition.
3. After service of notice, the respondent appeared before the court through its counsel and filed written statement contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.

It is contended that, there is no nexus between the death of Rathnamma HA and the bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-34-F-1445.
The deceased might have sustained injuries and succumbed to the same in a altogether accident, but

the petitioners with the sole intention to make an unlawful gain from the respondent, taking advantage of fact that the bus in question was operated on the said place on 01.11.2023, noting down the number of the bus, falsely implicated the bus in question and foisted false case against it in active collusion with the police.

The bus has not caused any accident on 01.11.2023, but on 09.11.2023 when the bus in question being operated in the schedule route, the police stopped the bus and forcibly took the driver stating the bus has caused the accident and falsely implicated the bus and filed false case against it.
The respondent has denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased.
It has also denied the amount spent towards the funeral expenses of the deceased.

It has denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-52-V-7991 in the accident and contended that the accident has occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle.

It is contended that the petition is bad for mis-joinder and non-joinder of necessary parties since for the alleged accident the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-V-7991 was solely responsible, consequently the owner and insurer of the same are necessary parties.
The respondent has further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners proves that they are the legal heirs of deceased Smt.
Rathnamma H.A.?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that on 01.11.2023 at about 2.15 p.m., when the deceased Rathnamma H.A. was proceeding on the motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-52-V-7991 as pillion rider near Kuluvanahalli village, Bengaluru- Tumkuru NH-48 Road, Nelamangala
, at that time, the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 34-F-1445 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased motor cycle from behind.
As a result of impact the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over her body and succumbed to the injuries on the spot as alleged by them?
3) Whether the respondent proves that the petition is bad for mis-joinder and non-joinder of necessary parties?

4) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ? If so, to what extent and from whom ?

7. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : In the Negative  Issue No.4 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.5 : As per final order for the  following :
 REASONS 8. Issue No.1:
The petitioner No.1 is stated to be the husband, petitioner No.2 and 3 stated to be the son and daughter of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 has filed affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Adhaar cards marked at Ex.P17 to 20 do fortify the said fact.
Hence this Tribunal hold that the petitioners No.1 to 3 are the legal heirs/representatives and dependents of deceased Rathnamma H.A.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
9. ISSUE NO.2 and 3:

It is the case of the petitioners that, on 01.11.2023 at about 2.15 p.m., when the deceased Rathnamma H.A. was proceeding on the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-V-7991 as pillion rider near Kuluvanahalli village, Bengaluru-Tumkuru NH-48 Road, Nelamangala, at that time, the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-34-F- 1445 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased motor cycle from behind.
As a result of impact the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over her body and succumbed to the injuries on the spot, and as such the respondent is liable to pay compensation to them.

10. In order to substantiate the contentions, petitioner No.1 stepped into the witness box and filed her affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, Spot mahazar,
seizure mahazar, Sketch, Inquest Report, statements of Shivaraju and Pavithra, PM Report, 133 notice and reply, IMV Report and Charge sheet at Ex.P1 to 16.

On the other hand, respondent has examined its driver as RW.1.
11.
This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of Bus.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.

There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order Nanjundappa vs Ksrtc on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90053061/
4 to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

12. According to the version of petitioners the accident happened near Kuluvanahalli village,
Bengaluru-Tumakuru NH-48 road, Nelamangala taluk, Bengaluru Rural district, when the deceased person was proceeding in a TVS Moped as a pillion rider, the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-34-F- 1445 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased's two wheeler and caused the accident.

On the other hand Respondent contention is that their bus not involved in the accident, petitioner colluding with police lodged a false complaint against the driver of bus and forcefully seized their bus and there is no dent or damages to their bus,
accident occurred due to the negligent act of the rider of the motor cycle.

Even the driver of the bus also tried to lodge a complaint but police have not received the same and to prove this contention respondent's bus driver examined as Rw1 but not produced any document to show whether he has tried to lodge a counter complaint.

RW1 in his cross examination stated that he has neither challenged the FIR or chargesheet before appropriate authority nor filed private complaint, any prudent man cannot sit silently without taking any action if he has no fault in the accident.
But the driver of the Bus has not taken any legal action.
Respondent another contention is that there is no damages to the bus, as per IMV report there is scratch mark on left side of the bus.
Bus is the heavy vehicle and it was hit to the small TVS Moped.
Damages are caused only to small vehicle and minor scratches to the heavy vehicle.
Therefore, the said contention of the Respondent is not tenable.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex . P.1
FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 to 6 which are the Spot Mahazar, Seizer Mahzar and Sketch prepared at the time of mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P3 it reflects that deceased was proceeding towards Tumakuru on NH-48 road as a pillion rider on the TVS Moped and suddenly the offending KSRTC bus came in a negligent manner from back side and hit deceased's Moped on the right side rear end,
due to the impact pillion rider fell down on the road.
If the driver of bus had come in a normal speed by observing ongoing vehicles who were playing on the road, then he could certainly avoid the accident.
Added more the contents of Ex.P15 IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more even the chargesheet as per Ex.P16 was also filed as against the driver of the bus.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3 to 6 coupled with Ex.P16 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence of the bus.

15. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of motor cycleist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even in the instant case though the driver of the bus is examined as RW.1 to show that there was no negligence on his part, even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the bus and he was charge sheeted.

6 16.
The petitioners with the help of Ex.P3 to 6 coupled with Ex.P16 clearly demonstrated that there was negligence on the part of offending vehicle driver.
Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA- 34-F-1445 by its driver.
In view of discussion made supra, with due respect to the decisions relied by the respondent, they are not helpful to his case.
the negligence is attributed on the driver of the bus and hence the question of joinder of owner and insurer of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-V-7991 as necessary parties does not arise at all.
Therefore, this Tribunal answers Issue No.2 in the Affirmative and Issue No.3 in the Negative.

Issue No.4:
17.

While answering issue No.2, I have already observed that the death of Rathnamma H.A., was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-34-F-1445.
It is stated that the deceased was aged 48 years at the time of the accident.
PW.1 has produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P17 which shows the date of birth as 08.04.1975.
The accident was occurred on 01.11.2023.
Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 48 years.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '13'.
18.
The petitioners have contended that the deceased was doing vegetable business and agriculture and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
In order to prove the same, petitioners have not produced any documents before the court.

Therefore, considering the occupation of the deceased and year of the accident, I deem it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/-
per month.

19. As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and she died at the age of 48 years.
Therefore, in this case, 25% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

If 25% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.20,000/- p.m. (Rs.16,000/- +
4,000/- i.e. 25%).
The deceased died leaving behind 3 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/3rd of her income is required to be deducted towards her personal expenses which comes to Rs.13,334/- p.m. (Rs.20,000 - Rs.6,666 = Rs.13,334/-).

Nanjundappa vs Ksrtc on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90053061/
7 20.
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.14,000/- p.m. and the multiplier '13' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.20,80,104/- (Rs.13,334 X 12 X 13).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.20,80,104/- under the head of loss of dependency.

21. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
22.

In this case, the petitioner No.2 and 3 are the major children of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners No.2 and 3 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of father/mother/son causes great shock and agony to the children and parents of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their mother.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 and 3 are entitled for Rs.96,800/-(Rs.48,400 x 2) under the head of Filial consortium.

23. In total, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of dependency 20,80,104/-

2. Towards loss of Consortium 48,400/-
to the petitioner No.1 3. Towards loss to estate 18,150/-
4. Towards transportation of 18,150/-
dead body funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses 5.

Towards loss of Filial 96,800/-
consortium to petitioner No.2 and 3(Rs.48,400 x 2) Total 22,61,604/-
In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.22,61,604/-.

8 24.
As regard the apportionment of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the petitioner is the husband and petitioner No.2 and 3 are son and daughter of the deceased.
Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 50:25:25 respectively.
25. The petitioners are claiming interest @ 9% per annum on the compensation amount.
The respondent has denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
26. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending KSRTC bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-34-F-1445.
It is not in dispute that respondent is not the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, it is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.4 Partly in the Affirmative.
27. Issue No.5:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.22,61,604/-(Rupees Twenty two lakhs sixty one thousand six hundred and four only) with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 50%
 Petitioner No.2 - 25%
 Petitioner No.3 - 25%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 to 3 a sum equal to 50% shall be deposited in their respective names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 2 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.

Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
